# Solution

## Setup

For each clearance level $a \in \{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$, I need the smallest positive integer using only digits $a$ and $a+1$ that is divisible by $99 = 9 \times 11$.

**Divisibility by 9:** The digit sum must be $\equiv 0 \pmod{9}$.

**Divisibility by 11:** The alternating sum (odd-position digits minus even-position digits, counting from the leftmost as position 1) must be $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$.

For an $n$-digit number with $p$ copies of digit $a$ and $q$ copies of digit $a+1$ ($p+q=n$), the digit sum is $ap + (a+1)q = an + q$.

---

## Case-by-case analysis

### $a=1$, digits $\{1,2\}$

Digit sum $= n + q$, range $[n, 2n]$. Need a multiple of 9 in this range.

- $n=5$: sum $= 9$ requires $q=4$ (four 2's, one 1). Alternating sum: 3 odd, 2 even positions. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} + \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 9$, so $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 9$. Need $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, but $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [3,6]$. No solution.
- $n=6,7,8$: sum $= 9$ is the only option; same modular obstruction ($\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, never in range). No solution.
- $n=9$: sum $= 9$ (all 1's) gives alternating sum $= 1$; sum $= 18$ (all 2's) gives alternating sum $= 2$. No.
- $n=10$: sum $= 18$ requires $q=8$ (eight 2's, two 1's). 5 odd, 5 even positions. $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 18 \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$ gives $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 9 \pmod{11}$, and $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} = 9 \in [5,10]$. ✓ This means one 1 and four 2's in odd positions, one 1 and four 2's in even positions. Smallest arrangement: 1 at position 1 (leading), 1 at position 10 (rightmost even).

$$X_1 = 1222222221, \quad \text{check: } 1{+}2{\cdot}8{+}1 = 18\equiv 0\pmod 9,\quad 1{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}1 = 0\equiv 0\pmod{11}.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=2$, digits $\{2,3\}$

Digit sum $= 2n + q$, range $[2n, 3n]$.

- $n=3$: sum $= 9$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333$. Alternating sum $= 3-3+3 = 3 \not\equiv 0$. No.
- $n=4$: sum $= 9$, three 2's + one 3. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, range $[4,6]$. No.
- $n=5$: no multiple of 9 in $[10,15]$.
- $n=6$: sum $= 18$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333333$. Alternating sum $= 3-3+3-3+3-3 = 0$. ✓

$$X_2 = 333333,\quad 333333/99 = 3367.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=3$, digits $\{3,4\}$

Digit sum $= 3n + q$, range $[3n, 4n]$.

- $n=3$: sum $= 9$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333$. Alternating sum $= 3$. No.
- $n=4$: no multiple of 9 in $[12,16]$.
- $n=5$: sum $= 18$, two 3's + three 4's. 3 odd, 2 even. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [9,12]$, need $= 9$ (for difference 0), but then $\text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 9$ with two digits from $\{3,4\}$: max $= 8$. Impossible. No.
- $n=6$: sum $= 18$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333333$. Alternating sum $= 0$. ✓

$$X_3 = 333333.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=4$, digits $\{4,5\}$

Digit sum $= 4n + q$, range $[4n, 5n]$.

- $n=1$: 4 or 5, not divisible by 9.
- $n=2$: sum $= 9$, one 4 + one 5. Options: 45 (alt. sum $= -1$), 54 (alt. sum $= 1$). Neither $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$. No.
- $n=3$: no multiple of 9 in $[12,15]$.
- $n=4$: sum $= 18$, two 4's + two 5's. 2 odd, 2 even. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} + \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 18$, need $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$. Difference $= 0 \Rightarrow \text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} = 9$, achievable as $4+5$. So one 4 and one 5 in each parity class. Smallest: position 1 $= 4$, position 2 $= 4$, position 3 $= 5$, position 4 $= 5$.

$$X_4 = 4455,\quad 4455/99 = 45.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=5$, digits $\{5,6\}$

Digit sum $= 5n + q$, range $[5n, 6n]$.

- $n=2$: no multiple of 9 in $[10,12]$.
- $n=3$: sum $= 18$, all 6's $\Rightarrow 666$. Alternating sum $= 6$. No.
- $n=4$: no multiple of 9 in $[20,24]$.
- $n=5$: sum $= 27$, three 5's + two 6's. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [15,18]$, need $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$ via $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 27 \equiv 0$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 8 \pmod{11}$, i.e., $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} = 8$ (too small) or $19$ (too big). No.
- $n=6$: sum $= 36$, all 6's $\Rightarrow 666666$. Alternating sum $= 0$. ✓

$$X_5 = 666666,\quad 666666/99 = 6734.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=6$, digits $\{6,7\}$

Digit sum $= 6n + q$, range $[6n, 7n]$.

- $n=3$: sum $= 18$, all 6's $\Rightarrow 666$. Alternating sum $= 6$. No.
- $n=4$: sum $= 27$, one 6 + three 7's. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [12,14]$, need $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 27 \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 8 \pmod{11}$, not in range. No.
- $n=5$: no multiple of 9 in $[30,35]$.
- $n=6$: sum $= 36$, all 6's $\Rightarrow 666666$. Alternating sum $= 0$. ✓

$$X_6 = 666666.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=7$, digits $\{7,8\}$

Digit sum $= 7n + q$, range $[7n, 8n]$.

- $n=2,3,4$: no multiple of 9 in the respective ranges.
- $n=5$: sum $= 36$, four 7's + one 8. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [21,24]$, need $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 36 \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 7 \pmod{11}$, not in range. No.
- $n=6$: sum $= 45$, three 7's + three 8's. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [21,24]$, need $\equiv 6 \pmod{11}$: not in range. No.
- $n=7$: sum $= 54$, two 7's + five 8's. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [28,32]$, need $\equiv 5 \pmod{11}$: not in range. No.
- $n=8$: sum $= 63$, one 7 + seven 8's. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [28,32]$, need $\equiv 5 \pmod{11}$: not in range. No.
- $n=9$: sum $= 63$ (all 7's, alt. sum $= 7$) or sum $= 72$ (all 8's, alt. sum $= 8$). No.
- $n=10$: sum $= 72$, eight 7's + two 8's. 5 odd, 5 even. $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 72 \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 3 \pmod{11}$, and $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} = 36 \in [35,40]$. ✓ One 8 + four 7's in odd positions, one 8 + four 7's in even positions. Smallest: 7 at position 1, 8's at positions 9 and 10.

$$X_7 = 7777777788,\quad 7777777788/99 = 78563412.\ \checkmark$$

The smallest value is $\boxed{4455}$, arising from clearance level $a=4$. # Solution

## Setup

For each clearance level $a \in \{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$, I need the smallest positive integer using only digits $a$ and $a+1$ that is divisible by $99 = 9 \times 11$.

**Divisibility by 9:** The digit sum must be $\equiv 0 \pmod{9}$.

**Divisibility by 11:** The alternating sum (odd-position digits minus even-position digits, counting from the leftmost as position 1) must be $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$.

For an $n$-digit number with $p$ copies of digit $a$ and $q$ copies of digit $a+1$ ($p+q=n$), the digit sum is $ap + (a+1)q = an + q$.

---

## Case-by-case analysis

### $a=1$, digits $\{1,2\}$

Digit sum $= n + q$, range $[n, 2n]$. Need a multiple of 9 in this range.

- $n=5$: sum $= 9$ requires $q=4$ (four 2's, one 1). Alternating sum: 3 odd, 2 even positions. $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} + \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 9$, so $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - \text{Sum}_{\text{even}} = 2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 9$. Need $\equiv 0 \pmod{11}$: $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, but $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \in [3,6]$. No solution.
- $n=6,7,8$: sum $= 9$ is the only option; same modular obstruction ($\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, never in range). No solution.
- $n=9$: sum $= 9$ (all 1's) gives alternating sum $= 1$; sum $= 18$ (all 2's) gives alternating sum $= 2$. No.
- $n=10$: sum $= 18$ requires $q=8$ (eight 2's, two 1's). 5 odd, 5 even positions. $2\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} - 18 \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$ gives $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} \equiv 9 \pmod{11}$, and $\text{Sum}_{\text{odd}} = 9 \in [5,10]$. ✓ This means one 1 and four 2's in odd positions, one 1 and four 2's in even positions. Smallest arrangement: 1 at position 1 (leading), 1 at position 10 (rightmost even).

$$X_1 = 1222222221, \quad \text{check: } 1{+}2{\cdot}8{+}1 = 18\equiv 0\pmod 9,\quad 1{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}2{+}2{-}1 = 0\equiv 0\pmod{11}.\ \checkmark$$

### $a=2$, digits $\{2,3\}$

Digit sum $= 2n + q$, range $[2n, 3n]$.

- $n=3$: sum $= 9$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333$. Alternating sum $= 3-3+3 = 3 \not\equiv 0$. No.

- $n=6$: sum $= 18$, all 3's $\Rightarrow 333333$. Alternating sum $= 3-3+3-3+3-3 = 0$. ✓
